gaps.sentence: The new model has ___ moving parts, so it breaks down less often.
gaps.explanation: 'Fewer moving parts' is correct because 'parts' is countable and plural.

gaps.sentence: A ___ of people object to the plans.
gaps.explanation: 'A large number of people' is correct for countables; 'a great deal of people' and 'an amount of people' are wrong.

gaps.sentence: ___ the information you gave was correct.
gaps.explanation: 'All the information' is correct; 'none/neither' would need 'of' and 'both' requires two separate countable items.

gaps.sentence: We can take the ferry or the tunnel — ___ way takes about three hours.
gaps.hint: one of two options, singular noun
gaps.explanation: 'Either way' means whichever of the two you choose; 'both' would need 'ways'.

gaps.sentence: It took a great ___ of courage to admit the mistake.
gaps.explanation: 'A great deal of courage' is the standard pattern with uncountables; 'a great number of' needs countables.

gaps.sentence: Don't rush — we've got ___ of time.
gaps.hint: fixed pattern: ___ of time (no article needed)
gaps.explanation: 'Plenty of time' needs no article; 'lot of time' would need 'a', and 'much of time' needs 'the'.
'Far too much information' is the correct intensifier pattern; 'far much' and 'far very' do not exist.

gaps.hint: an unspecified day in the future
gaps.explanation: 'Another day' means some other, unspecified day; 'the other day' refers to the recent past.
